newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen-Krupp make concrete plans to secure jobs.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen-Krupp make concrete plans to secure jobs.

text.p: Thyssen and Krupp have devised concrete plans to secure two-thirds of the 1,300 new jobs promised to offset cuts connected with the recent merger of their steel operations, the companies said.
For the remaining one-third, there are well-based plans that will be made more specific in coming months, they said.
The closure of part of the Dortmund steel works will cost up to 4,000 jobs.
Thyssen AG promised to create 800 new jobs in the region by the year 2001, while Krupp promised 500.
Thyssen plans to create new jobs by building a stainless steel service center in Dortmund, two freight centers, and a construction warehouse.
Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp plans to invest in new production and assembly lines for steel construction parts and broadening its activities in raw materials and recycling.
IG Metall union officials approved the plans and were due to present them to their members on Tuesday.

"All concerned are sure it will be possible to create the promised jobs by 2001. This will make a great contribution toward offseting the jobs lost in the Dortmund region through the steel merger," the companies said.
